questions.question: Best first step automating a risky network change in Python?
options: Separate intent validation + dry-run/diff against live state before any write; never mix discover-and-mutate in one opaque shot
questions.explanation: Safe automation patterns beat clever scripts.

questions.question: Shell one-liners in production automation—manager stance:
options: Fine for glue; dangerous as the system of record—prefer reviewed, tested code with clear exit codes and idempotency

questions.question: Perl still appears in network tooling. Fair take:
options: Legacy reality—stabilize, wrap, or migrate deliberately; don't rewrite working glue mid-incident without cause

questions.question: Prefer device API/NETCONF/gNMI over screen-scraping CLI when:
options: You need stable structured data and safer transactions—scraping breaks on banner/format changes

questions.question: Secrets in automation:
options: Use a vault/secret manager; never commit credentials; short-lived tokens where possible

questions.question: Idempotent automation means:
options: Re-running converges to the same desired state without stacking duplicate changes

questions.question: Parsing CLI with regex in prod—risk:
options: Format drift causes silent mis-parse—prefer structured encodings or golden parsers with tests

questions.question: Pushing config to 5000 boxes concurrently without limits:
options: Can melt control planes/AAA—use pools, backoff, blast-radius budgets, and health gates

questions.question: Unit test vs lab soak for network automation:
options: Unit-test pure logic; integration-test against lab/cOS images; canary in prod—don't skip layers

questions.question: Script fails halfway through a change window. Good design:
options: Checkpointed, reversible steps with clear rollback and inventory of completed nodes
questions.explanation: Partial failure is the normal case.

questions.question: Using vendor SDK vs raw requests:
options: SDKs speed correct auth/pagination—still understand the API and handle rate limits/timeouts

questions.question: Inventory source of truth should be:
options: Authoritative DB/CMDB/Git-backed inventory—not tribal knowledge in a wiki paste

questions.question: Dry-run that doesn't read live state is weak because:
options: It cannot detect drift or conflicting reality—compare intended vs actual

questions.question: Automation logs should include:
options: Who/what/when, target set, before/after or diff, success/fail per node—enough for RCA

questions.question: Network device APIs hang—your code should:
options: Bound timeouts, retries with jitter, and circuit-break unhealthy targets

questions.question: Migrating a Perl collector to Python—order:
options: Characterize outputs/SLAs; parity tests; dual-run; cut over; retire—don't big-bang rewrite

questions.question: Bash scripts in CI should use:
options: set -euo pipefail (or equivalent discipline), quoted vars, and explicit error paths

questions.question: Generating device config from templates—key risk:
options: Incorrect assumptions → widespread wrong config; validate rendered output and peer review templates

questions.question: CLI automation libraries still need:
options: Prompt handling, paging, privilege modes, and idempotent intent—library ≠ safe change process

questions.question: After an automated push, verify with:
options: Telemetry/probes/canaries tied to customer impact—not only 'API returned 200'
